sections.title: High: fix before anyone else uses it
sections.intro: The full report is docs/plans/security-review-2026-11-21.md (7 high, 14 medium, 12 low). I checked the ✔ items by hand. Nothing has been changed yet. Each answer says how I'd fix it; pick one, or say leave it.

questions.question: Signed-in members get **everyone's** live events: notifications, approvals with tool args, pairing codes and session lists. They can also subscribe to any session id and read its chat live. How should this be fixed?
questions.content: `core/src/web.ts:446` guards `on.user` and `on.session` with sign-in only. `api/events.ts` emits notifications and approvals to all of `on.user`.

options.label: Scope events per person
options.description: `on.user` gets a `{ user }` param that must match the subscriber. Notifications and approvals go only to their person or approvers, and session summaries only to people who can see the session. `on.session` checks `visibleSession`. Sockets close on sign-out or disable.

options.label: Admin-only for now
options.description: Keep the channels, but only admins may subscribe until per-person scoping is built. Members lose live updates.

questions.why: This is the one finding that leaks between people with no injection needed.

questions.question: `z.url()` accepts `javascript:`. A malicious MCP server's OAuth metadata, a `Link`, or a model's `web/read` URL can run script on the hub when clicked. Should I add one `safeHref` check everywhere?
questions.content: ConnectPage `location.assign`, PeopleSignIn SSO test, LinkCard, ThreadPane `window.open`, web ReadView/SearchView/CrawlSummary. Schemas: `link.ts:449` connectStart url, `resources.ts:150` Link.url; ayepi oauth2 metadata endpoints are bare `z.string()`.

options.label: Schema + UI
options.description: Add an `HttpUrl` zod type (http/https only) in core for connectStart and Link. Export a `safeHref` from the SDK and use it for every data-built `:href` and `window.open`. ayepi's OAuth metadata requires https endpoints (on the local harness branch).

questions.question: Renderers are trusted (decided). But a newly paired system's client build and config component may load on PairPage and ReviewView **before** it is reviewed. Should system browser code wait for approval?
questions.content: `serve.ts:137` only withholds builds that are switched off or in a pending review. `config-component.ts:101` does same-origin `import()`. PairPage says nothing is used until review.

options.label: Load only after approval
options.description: `/clients/*` and the config component refuse a system whose client build hasn't been approved in a review. PairPage shows a plain placeholder until then. I'll add a test for the first pairing.

options.label: Also sandbox system UI
options.description: Wait for approval, and also move config components (not chat renderers) into a sandboxed iframe on a separate origin. This takes much more work.

questions.question: When you run an agent fn directly with `!`, its tool calls count as **you** calling them. A prompt-injected agent can then write, delete or run admin fns with no approval card. Fix?
questions.content: `execution/agent.ts:724`: `#agentActor` falls back to `run.caller`. `policies.ts:178` allows the call when `caller === turnUser`.

options.label: Always an agent actor
options.description: `#agentActor` creates (and caches) the agent actor for any agent fn instead of falling back to the person, so its tool calls go through the normal agent approvals.

questions.question: With no approval, the fs bash safe list can `cat` any file outside the roots (fs's own private key, ~/.ssh, other systems' state). It can also read `.env` via `$PWD/.env` and print API keys with `echo $VAR`. Fix?
questions.content: `fs/server/env.ts:13` SAFE prefixes; `shell.ts:25` prefix match; `shell.ts:155` passes the full `process.env`; `sensitive.ts:410` skips words with `$`.

options.label: Confine + scrub
options.description: A safe command is safe only if every path word resolves inside the roots and has no `$`, `~` or glob. Otherwise it asks. Bash starts with `scrubbedEnv` (plus an admin allowlist). `echo` leaves the safe list.

options.label: Confine + OS sandbox
options.description: The above, plus running bash in an OS sandbox restricted to the roots (Windows: a restricted token or job object). This is much more work.

options.label: Drop the safe list
options.description: Every bash command asks.

questions.question: `fs/write` on `.git/config` (fsmonitor), `package.json` or a test config turns into code execution through the git hook or `npm test` / `npx vitest` on the safe list. Fix?

options.label: Ask + harden git
options.description: Writes to `.git/**`, `package.json`, `*.config.*` and hook folders ask by default. Internal git runs with `-c core.fsmonitor= -c core.hooksPath=` and no system config. `npm test`, `npx vitest` and `npx tsc` leave the safe list. Git safe entries become exact shapes (no `--output`, `-D`, `-f`) (also covers M13).

questions.question: The api system lets a model add a service at any base URL (localhost, 169.254.169.254, the hub's port, the LAN) and reads the response back. Apply the SDK's address guard?

options.label: Guard, admin allow-private
options.description: `addressVerdict` runs on every hop and on the openapi fetch. Private and loopback base URLs are refused unless an admin enabled them per service. Model-added services need approval and are visible only to their creator until an admin shares them (also covers M9 squatting).

sections.title: Medium and low
sections.intro: Grouped so you can pick in bulk. Details and file references for each are in the report, under Medium and Low.

questions.question: Which web-side fixes should I make?

options.label: M3 CSP + frame-ancestors + nosniff
options.description: `frame-ancestors 'none'`, nosniff, CSP `script-src 'self'` on index.html; non-JS `/clients/*` files sent as attachments.

options.label: M4 outside images click-to-load
options.description: Markdown images from other hosts show a placeholder until clicked (no-referrer). Hub and resource images load as now.

options.label: M2 bind the SSO hand-off
options.description: A single-use code tied to the `harness_sso` cookie replaces the refresh token in the fragment.

options.label: M1 setup token for first admin
options.description: With no env admin, `createAdmin` needs a one-time token printed to the hub log.

options.label: M12 per-IP sign-in limit
options.description: Add a per-address limiter. Failures for an email slow it down instead of locking it out.

questions.question: Which link and fleet fixes should I make?

options.label: M5 pairing rate limits, real socket IP
options.description: `X-Forwarded-For` is trusted only with a trusted-proxy setting. Re-keying an existing system needs a token, not a code.

options.label: M7 hub proves itself
options.description: Pin the hub's key at pairing and sign the challenge reply. Require wss for non-loopback links. This is bigger work.

options.label: Low: reserved names + no shell on install

questions.question: Which system-level fixes should I make?

options.label: M10 Chrome: block ws/service workers, pin DNS
M11 Claude: approve weaker modes, user-only settings for probes, realpath
options.description: Switching a session to `auto` or `acceptEdits` always shows a card. `importables` probes with `settingSources: ['user']`. The MCP import card previews the command.

options.label: M14 grep in a worker with a deadline
Low: pin MCP OAuth token endpoint
Low: CLI secrets via env/stdin, no cwd .env URL with admin creds

questions.question: `web/read`, `fetch_raw` and `crawl` are read-only and need no approval, so an injected model can put secrets in a URL and send them out. What should happen?

options.label: Ask for new domains in a session
options.description: The first fetch to a domain the person hasn't used or named in the session asks. Later fetches there don't.

options.label: Just log them
options.description: Keep reads free, and show outgoing URLs on the run so they can be checked afterwards. H1–H7 remove most ways to reach secrets in the first place.

questions.question: How should I build the fixes you pick?

options.label: One workflow, high first
options.description: High fixes first, each with a test, then the rest. I verify, commit locally (no push), and send you a hitloop review of the diff.
